lesson.title: Read the picture-graph key
lesson.subtitle: Full symbols and a shared key
lesson.story: This picture graph shows items in pretend collections. Each full symbol represents 2 items. These are example data, not a class survey.
lesson.objective: Use a picture-graph key to find a category quantity.

steps.title: Read the key
steps.prompt: How many items does one full symbol represent?
hints: Find the key above the rows.
Look beside the single symbol in the key.
The key applies to every full symbol.
The key says one full symbol represents 2 items.

steps.title: Count full symbols
steps.prompt: How many full symbols are in the Apples row?
hints: The key tells items, but here we count symbols.
There are 4 full symbols in the named row.

steps.title: Read a category
steps.prompt: How many items does Apples represent?
hints: Using the full symbols and the key gives 8 items.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why must we use the key?

choices.label: The key tells us how many items each symbol stands for.
Each symbol stands for just one item, whatever the key says.
A half symbol can always be counted as one whole item too.

hints: One symbol can represent more than one item.
Every row uses the same key.
The key tells us how many items each symbol stands for.
